The CodeQL database maltrail-db was created from the same tree (sourceLocationPrefix matches, creation sha bb4d24b), so file/line evidence below is verified against the database snapshot.

target.projectDescription: Malicious traffic detection system: a sensor that sniffs network packets (pcapy) and matches them against trails, a server (custom BaseHTTPRequestHandler HTTPD) that serves logs/events to a browser UI, and a trail update mechanism that fetches feeds over HTTP. Python 2/3 compatible via a vendored thirdparty/six.

framework.notes: No web framework detected. All framework scores are below the 0.50 threshold, so no framework reference is loaded. The externally reachable attack surface is built directly on the standard library through the vendored thirdparty.six compatibility layer: a hand-rolled BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass (core/httpd.py) for the server, pcapy for packet capture on the sensor, optparse for CLIs, urllib for feed fetching. Source/sink shapes below are derived from repository evidence per references/python.md and references/patterns.md (language reference path, since no framework reference matches).

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) the HTTP server port: query string, POST body, headers, cookies and client address flow into params and handler state, and params.get("username") is interpolated into a shell command at core/httpd.py:399; (2) the network wire seen by the sensor: packet bytes via pcapy are unpacked and matched; (3) the filesystem: configuration file, trails file, log files, whitelists; (4) CLI arguments/environment of the sensor/server/update processes; (5) remote feed servers through urllib. Command execution sinks are subprocess.check_output/subprocess.Popen with shell=True; the only one whose command string is dynamically formatted from request-derived values is core/httpd.py:399.

sanitizerObservations: core/httpd.py:399 sits after a login-validity check (valid user with sha256 hash + one-time nonce at :320-336), but the executed command string itself is not quoted or escaped; params.get("username") is inserted verbatim into the logger command

no shlex.quote / pipes.quote / shell-escaping wrapper exists anywhere in project source
core/httpd.py:509 '".." in dates' guards the events log path against traversal (path-domain sanitizer, not command-domain)
the sensor subprocess commands are built from static strings or internal numeric values (affinity/pid); no network-derived substitution was observed at sensor.py:1031-1037
inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: The static probe commands in core/settings.py (sysctl/vmstat/free/top) and the schedtool affinity command in sensor.py are platform-introspection commands with static or internally-derived operands; they are recorded as sink candidates only, not as vulnerabilities.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile followed by codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output is decoded directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name); catches dynamic or unresolved shapes that API graphs miss and is subject to name-collision noise. The vendored thirdparty.six.moves indirection (urllib/BaseHTTPServer imported as _urllib/_BaseHTTPServer) is invisible to API graphs, so the urllib parse/decode boundary is matched at AST level

exclusions: no test/fixture directories exist in this repository (nothing excluded on that ground)
logging-only helpers (log_message / log_error / print / sys.stderr.write / send_header / wfile.write) are not extracted as candidates; pure output sites are out of scope

maltrail-safe-db (a pristine copy shipped inside the source tree) is a duplicate reference tree, not an executed entry point; rows from it are not distinguished in the raw extraction but it contains no exec API or HTTP handler code

uncoveredCases: core/httpd.py:147 'content = getattr(self, "_%s" % path)(params)' - the handler method is selected dynamically from the request path. The dispatch is captured as an internal_transfer row (call whose callee is itself a getattr(...) call), and the _% handler methods of ReqHandler are captured by the param family, but the path->method binding itself is not resolvable.
core/httpd.py:202-204 'getattr(self, "_%s" % name.lower(), None)' - same dynamic-getattr shape for content tag substitution.

core/log.py:223 '_(event_tuple, packet)' - plugin functions are called through a loop variable loaded from config.plugin_functions (populated by __import__ at sensor.py:954); the element call is not resolvable. Mitigated by the plugin(event_tuple, packet) parameter rows in plugins/*.py and the log_event parameter rows.

sensor.py:954 'module = __import__(filename[:-3])' - dynamic plugin import driven by the -p CLI value; not resolvable, mitigated by the cli family (parser.add_option '-p') and plugin function parameters.

core/settings.py:289 'value.replace(match.group(0), os.environ.get(match.group(1), match.group(0)))' - $VAR interpolation inside config values; the root os.environ.get read is captured, the string blending is not.

Bare-name (from-import) execution sinks are only matched for distinctive names (system, popen, getoutput, getstatusoutput); bare call/run/check_call are too collision-prone. In this repository every subprocess site is attribute-qualified (subprocess.check_output / subprocess.Popen), so this gap is not exercised.

six compatibility layer: httpd.py imports BaseHTTPServer/urllib via thirdparty.six.moves aliases, so API-graph resolution of parse_qs/unquote_plus/urlopen is not expected; those boundaries rely on the ast match_kind (module prefix _urllib/urllib or bare from-imported names).
